title: Agreement that images are adored properly—but split on whether the image alone can be integral object
source_text: XLI. Sed quamvis recentiores in eo consentiant, imagines proprie & vere adorandas esse, nihilominus inter eos controvertitur quis sit illius adorationis modus atque ratio. Fatentur quidem illi omnes imagines non debere adorari propter se, sed tantum propter exemplar quod repraesentant, & cujus similitudinem gerunt. Sed quaestio est, An, licet imago propter exemplar adoretur, tamen per se, & in se possit esse integrum objectum adorationis, ita ut adoretur adoratione diversa ab ea qua ipsum exemplar adoratur, & quae sic terminetur in ipsam imaginem, ut ejus materia proxima & immediata sit imago sola, non autem exemplar. Quemadmodum Legatus Regis honoratur propter Regem cujus nomine Legationem obit, sed tamen potest & solet honorari, honore cujus ipse terminus proximus est, & quo Rex, directe saltem, non honoratur, ac proinde qui est diversus ab eo, & inferior eo quo Rex ipse honorandus est.
pass_a_gloss: But although the more recent agree in this, that images are to be adored properly and truly, nevertheless among them it is controverted what is the mode and reason of that adoration. They all grant indeed that images ought not to be adored on account of themselves, but only on account of the exemplar which they represent, and whose likeness they bear. But the question is, Whether, although the image is adored on account of the exemplar, yet per se and in itself it can be an integral object of adoration, so that it is adored with an adoration diverse from that by which the exemplar itself is adored, and which is so terminated in the image itself that its proximate and immediate matter is the image alone, not the exemplar. Just as a King's legate is honored on account of the King in whose name he carries out the Legation, yet can and is accustomed to be honored with an honor of which he himself is the proximate terminus, and with which the King, at least directly, is not honored, and which accordingly is diverse from, and inferior to, that with which the King himself is to be honored.
pass_b_english: Recent Schoolmen agree images are properly adored, but quarrel over the mode.
All say images are not adored for themselves but for the exemplar.
The live question: can the image alone be an integral, proximate object of a distinct adoration—like a legate honored for the king yet with his own inferior honor?

choices.why: The represented person or thing, not a mere model.
